occurrences.source_excerpt: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 1: Minor • slight damage to cartilage +/- osteophytes • NO apparent narrowing of joint space (normal at X-ray) • Asymptomatic (NO pain / discomfort) Stage 2: Mild • some symptoms noted like joint stiffness & pain, esp. after prolonged sitting • X-ray:clearly shown growth of osteophytes, cartilage begin to get thin

occurrences.source_excerpt: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 3: Moderate • moderate narrow joint space, with cartilage loss • thickening of bone just underneath cartilage • pain & discomfort with daily activities like walking, bending • joint inflammation - excess synovial fluid • increase swelling

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 4: Severe • further joint space narrowing, with continuous cartilage loss • more significant pain & discomfort with daily activities due to joint friction • X-ray: bone on bone (cartilage completely worn / little left) • Deformity with varus (bow leg) or valgus (knock knee)

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) • Relative uncommon rheumatic disease that affect the spine • Prevalence: • Global – 0.1-1.4% [Dean et al, 2014] • Hong Kong – 0.2-0.3% [Zhu et al, 2008] • long-term condition related to autoimmune disease • Joints and ligaments of spine and other areas of the body become inflamed • e.g. sacroiliac joint, hips, shoulders • May involve other organs such as eyes, lungs, heart

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Treatment: • No cure for AS, treatment available to relieve the symptoms and delay progression • Medications to reduce pain & inflammation: • NSAIDS • DMARDs, Biologics • Corticosteriods • Exercises: reduce pain & stiffness • Physiotherapy: improve posture, flexibility, joint mobility • Surgery: for rare cases to repair significantly damaged joints or correct severe bends in spine

occurrences.source_excerpt: Signs & symptoms – Joints • Joint pain, tenderness, swelling, redness or stiffness > 6 weeks • Morning stiffness for > 1 hour • > ONE joint are affected • Small joints are commonly affected – Hands, Wrists & toes • Symmetrical joint pain: on both sides of the body • Decrease joint range of motion (ROM) • Joint deformity Flare - a period of high disease activity, last for days/months ** increases in inflammation & other symptoms
